messages.subject: Multilevel model convergence issues
parts:
I am trying to fit a multilevel model of the form,

model{
  for(i in 1:N){
    int aCountry;
    aCountry = country[i];
    vote[i] ~ bernoulli_logit(alpha[aCountry] + beta_g[aCountry] * gender[i] + beta_a[aCountry] * age[i] + beta_r[aCountry] * rlgblg[i]);
  }
  alpha_raw ~ normal(0,1);
  beta_a_raw ~ normal(0,1);
  gamma ~ normal(0,1);
  gamma1 ~ normal(0,1);
  
  ##...other priors
}

where I allow the alpha and beta_a to be determined hierarchically (in a non-centred way),

transformed parameters{
  real alpha[K];
  real beta_a[K];
  for(i in 1:K){
    alpha[i] = alpha_top +  gamma * democracy[i] + alpha_sigma * alpha_raw[i];
    beta_a[i] = beta_a_top + gamma1 * gdpPerCapita[i] + beta_a_sigma * beta_a_raw[i];
  }
}

such that, alpha_i ~ N(alpha_top+gamma * democracy_i, alpha_sigma) and beta_a_i ~ N(beta_a_top + gamma1 * gdpPerCapita_i, beta_a_sigma).

The model works fine when I just have the hierarchy for alpha, but completely fails to run when I include the gamma1 * gdpPerCapita_i term in the hierarchical prior for beta_a_i. 

I have tried setting more informative priors on gamma1 but things still fail to converge. There is basically no mixing of the chains whatsoever! Does anyone have an idea how I can diagnose what is going wrong? I am a bit at wits-end here.

Best,

Ben

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Multilevel model convergence issues
parts:
It really helps to see the whole model. I wish we could
somehow flash our instructions for bug reporting up before
users write messages to the list. Which version of Stan
and which version of which interface you're using will help
as will a complete dump of any error messages you're getting.

If you run RStan, just run one chain and then you'll see the
messages without having to do anything special (or ask the RStan
devs how to get things out of more chains---I don't know how to
do it).

- Bob
